correctness.rationale: For B>d, degree-d monomials have pairwise distinct weights under the diagonal action with variable weights B^j, by uniqueness of base-B expansion. Hence the ambient projective fixed locus is precisely the set of degree-d monomial lines. Every such monomial can be split into blocks of sizes d_1,...,d_r, so every ambient fixed point lies in the prescribed factorization variety. The restricted fixed locus is therefore exactly all binomial(d+m-1,m-1) monomial points. Euler localization for a projective algebraic C* action, proved in the package by a Rosenlicht-stratification argument, gives the claimed Euler characteristic without smoothness assumptions. The checker independently verifies weight separation and prescribed-degree monomial factorizations over all tested partitions.

value.rationale: Varieties of reducible forms are classical parameter spaces whose dimensions, secants, and singular geometry depend substantially on the partition of the degree. The theorem shows that a basic global topological invariant is nevertheless completely insensitive to this factorization data and, for m>=3, even equals the Euler characteristic of the strictly larger ambient projective space. This is a natural all-partition structural classification and identifies a precise limitation of Euler characteristic in detecting reducibility type.
